## Why reuse public data? {#why}

- A **control** for your own experiment
- A **new question** asked of an old dataset
- A **practice dataset** for learning a pipeline
- Cheap: someone else already sequenced it

. . .

The catch: getting the files out is less obvious than it should be.

::: {.notes}
Ask the room: who has tried to download data from a paper? What went wrong?
:::

## The databases {#databases}

| Database | Run by | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| **GEO** | NCBI (USA) | Experiment descriptions, sample info, **processed** files |
| **SRA** | NCBI (USA) | **Raw reads** (NCBI's `.sra` format) |
| **ENA** | EMBL-EBI (UK) | Raw reads, also as ready-made **`.fastq.gz`** |
| DDBJ | Japan | Raw reads |
| dbGaP / EGA | NCBI / EBI | **Controlled-access** human data |

SRA, ENA and DDBJ **mirror each other** (INSDC): any run is in all three.

::: {.book-link}
[The databases](../chapters/databases.html)
:::

## GEO hands raw reads to SRA {#geo-sra}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart TD
  GSE["GEO series GSE52778<br/>(the experiment)"] --> GSM1["GSM1275862<br/>N61311_untreated"]
  GSE --> GSM2["GSM1275863<br/>N61311_Dex"]
  GSE -.-> SUP["processed files"]
  GSM1 --> SRX1["SRX384345"] --> SRR1["SRR1039508"]
  GSM2 --> SRX2["SRX384346"] --> SRR2["SRR1039509"]
```

## Processed or raw? {#processed-or-raw}

| You want to… | Download |
|---|---|
| Re-plot their result, view their tracks | **GEO supplementary files** (no toolkit) |
| Compare with your data, processed the same way | **Raw reads** |
| Use a newer genome or annotation | Raw reads |
| Check their QC | Raw reads |

Processing differences between labs can be bigger than the biology.

## SRA Normalized vs SRA Lite {#sra-lite}

| | Normalized (`.sra`) | Lite (`.sralite`) |
|---|---|---|
| Quality scores | Original | **Constant**: 30 (pass) or 3 (reject) |
| Size | Larger | ~60 % smaller |
| Fine for | Everything | Counting genes, calling peaks |

FastQC quality plot **flat at 30**? That's Lite data, not a perfect run.

## Sample, library, run {#sample-library-run}

```{mermaid}
%%{init: {"htmlLabels": false, "flowchart": {"htmlLabels": false}}}%%
flowchart LR
  S["Sample<br/>biological material<br/>GSM · SRS · SAMN"] -->|"library prep"| L["Library<br/>tube of fragments<br/>SRX"] -->|"sequencing"| R["Run<br/>batch of reads<br/>SRR"]
```

| | Sample | Library | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Several per parent? | — | yes (two preps; RNA + ATAC) | yes (lanes, top-ups) |
| Replicates? | **biological** | technical | **not** replicates |
| Before analysis | keep separate | usually merge | **always merge** |

Different pipette tip → different sample or library. Different lane → same library.

::: {.book-link}
[Accessions](../chapters/accessions.html#sample-library-run)
:::

## Accessions, decoded {#accessions}

| Level | GEO | SRA | ENA | BioProject / BioSample |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project | `GSE` | `SRP` | `ERP` | `PRJNA`, `PRJEB` |
| Sample | `GSM` | `SRS` | `ERS` | `SAMN`, `SAMEA` |
| Library | | `SRX` | `ERX` | |
| **Run** | | **`SRR`** | **`ERR`** | |

**Runs are what you download.** One sample can have many runs: merge them.

## Quick check {#quiz}

Three dishes of cells, one library each, each library sequenced on two lanes.

- How many samples? libraries? runs?
- How many samplesheet rows?

. . .

**3 samples, 3 libraries, 6 runs → 3 rows** (join the two lanes first).

## Finding the runs: SRA Run Selector {#finding-the-runs}

1. Paper → **data availability** → `GSE52778`
2. GEO page → scroll to **Samples**
3. Bottom of the page: *Relations → SRA* → **Run Selector**\
   (or `ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/study/?acc=GSE52778`)
4. Download **Metadata** (`SraRunTable.csv`) and **Accession List** (`SRR_Acc_List.txt`)\
   (**Total** row = all runs; **Selected** row = the ticked ones)

::: {.notes}
Live: open GEO, then Run Selector. Point at Run, Experiment, BioSample,
LibraryLayout, AvgSpotLen, Bytes.
:::

## Where the two files go {#where-files-go}

```
~/download-public-data/      ← the scripts, cloned once
~/public_data/               ← cluster: in scratch
└── GSE52778/                ← ONE folder per dataset; run every command here
    ├── SRR_Acc_List.txt     ← "Accession List"
    ├── SraRunTable.csv      ← "Metadata"
    └── fastq/ merged/ ...   ← made by the download
```

## Moving them into place {#moving-files}

```bash
# working on this computer
mkdir -p ~/public_data/GSE52778 && cd ~/public_data/GSE52778
mv ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv .

# working on a cluster: run this ON YOUR LAPTOP
scp ~/Downloads/SRR_Acc_List.txt ~/Downloads/SraRunTable.csv \
    <user>@<cluster>:/scratch/<user>/public_data/GSE52778/

# then check
wc -l SRR_Acc_List.txt; head -3 SRR_Acc_List.txt; head -2 SraRunTable.csv
```

Downloaded twice? Browsers save `SRR_Acc_List (1).txt`: rename as you move.

## Columns that matter {#runtable}

| Column | Why |
|---|---|
| `Run` | What you download |
| `BioSample`, `Sample Name`, `GEO_Accession` | Which sample (several runs can share one) |
| `LibraryLayout` | `PAIRED` or `SINGLE` |
| `AvgSpotLen` | Read 1 + read 2 (126 = 2 × 63) |
| `Bytes` | Plan disk space |
| `treatment`, `cell_line`, … | The biology (names vary) |

**Save `SraRunTable.csv` with your data.** It's your samplesheet's source.

## The same thing, from ENA or the command line {#ena-cli}

```bash
# ENA: one table, with direct FASTQ links and MD5s
curl -s "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport?accession=SRP033351&result=read_run&fields=run_accession,sample_title,library_layout,read_count,fastq_ftp,fastq_md5&format=tsv"

# NCBI Entrez Direct
esearch -db sra -query PRJNA229998 | efetch -format runinfo > runinfo.csv

# pysradb
pysradb metadata SRP033351 --detailed
```

## Before you download: checklist {#checklist}

- [ ] Right assay (`LibraryStrategy`, the GEO design)
- [ ] Which runs belong to which sample
- [ ] Paired or single-end; read length
- [ ] Library kit / strandedness, if stated
- [ ] Disk: **10–20×** the summed `Bytes`, free
- [ ] Open access (not dbGaP / EGA)

## Recap {#recap}

1. **GEO** describes; **SRA / ENA** store the reads.
2. **Sample → library → run.** Download runs; merge runs of one library.
3. Save **`SraRunTable.csv`** and **`SRR_Acc_List.txt`** at the top of **one
   folder per dataset**, and run everything from there.

Next deck: getting the reads onto your disk, and checking them.
